maya: Heads-up — while onboarding helix-8b I hit a reproducible decoding divergence after q4 quantization when KV caching is enabled. Float32 baseline looks fine.

arjun: ugh. can you paste a minimal repro? batch size / seq len?

maya: repro below. single-shot generation with prefix length 64 then stream 1 token at a time. divergence shows up by token ~12.
```
# repro
python -m rwi_inference.run \\
  --model helix-8b --quant q4_0 --kv-cache on \\
  --seed 42 --prompt-file tests/prompts/short_dialogue.txt \\
  --batch 1 --gen-steps 32
```

jenna: did you try q8 and fp16?

maya: q8 and fp16 both match fp32 up to 32 tokens. only q4 diverges. q4 with kv off also matches fp32. so it's an interaction: q4 + kv.

liam: possible suspects: 1) rounding/accum errors in quantized matmuls for KV write/read, 2) mis-applied rotary freq scaling for cached positions, or 3) buffer overwrite when streaming.

arjun: inline check: compare KV tensors across steps between fp32 and q4 run. if they differ right after write, suspect quant write. can you dump `kv.{layer}.{step}.npy`?

maya: attaching small diff excerpt (pasted values):
```
# layer 5 kv write step 3
fp32[0:6] = [0.1234, -0.0456, 0.0001, 0.0013, -0.0009, 0.0022]
q4_dequant[0:6] = [0.1230, -0.0457, -0.0004, 0.0011, -0.0013, 0.0019]
```
Differences small but accumulate.

jenna: small diffs ok usually but accumulation + rotary can amplify. check rotary cos/sin application: are we reusing cached sin_cos for absolute positions vs relative?

liam: good point — our runtime stores sin_cos per cache index and applies offset on read. if quantization changes scale of K/V slightly, the dot-prod distribution shifts -> softer softmax -> different attention -> cascade.

arjun: test idea: force deterministic rounding (higher precision path) for the q4 runtime for the KV write/read path only. if divergence disappears, it's quant math.

maya: tried `--force-high-precision-kv` flag locally, divergence goes away.

jenna: then next steps: 1) add a small compensating scale/biased dequant for KV write path and run nli/llama-eval suite, 2) run through our eval regressions (toxicity/qa/translation) to check for quality regressions, 3) try different q4 schemes (per-channel, symmetric) to see which reduces drift.

liam: also add a runtime unit test that streams generation and asserts logits at token 12 are within epsilon of fp32 for the baseline prompt. ci-bot: can you spin a quick flaky job?

ci-bot: CI job queued: rwi-helix8b-kv-q4-smoke #1427. logs: https://ci.redwood/1427 (will post artifacts kv dumps).

arjun: I'll own the kernel side (matmul dequant path). maya please collect exact layer diffs for first 8 layers and upload. jenna can you run the eval battery once we have a candidate fix? liam please add streaming unit and a small stress test for batch>1 boundaries.

maya: uploaded diffs to /artifacts/helix8b/q4-kv-diffs.tar.gz and linked in CI. also included the small prompt set that reproduces across seeds.

jenna: timeline?

arjun: aim for an initial patch (deterministic dequant for KV writes) today — if green, we'll run the eval suite overnight. liam will add unit test + stress tomorrow morning.

liam: adding note: watch out for perf regressions from higher-precision path. if perf hits >10% token/sec slowdown we need an adaptive path: high-precision only for write then cast back.

maya: ok. I'll run the eval suite next and post quality diffs. also add a test comparing rotary sin_cos indices between fp32 and q4 — to confirm no index drift.

arjun: good. if hypothesis holds, long-term fix is to refine q4 dequant algorithm or switch KV storage to a slightly higher precision (q8) while keeping compute q4. we'll present perf/quality tradeoffs.

jenna: thumbs-up. ping me when CI artifacts are in. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: rwi-helix8b-kv-q4-smoke #1427 finished — artifacts uploaded: /artifacts/ci/1427/ (kv dumps, logs, perf). status: flaky (1/3 failures).

maya: artifacts look consistent with local. filing intake ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RWI-1182 (summary: helix-8b q4+kv decoding drift). includes reproduction steps, diffs, owners.

arjun: cool. we'll iterate there. thanks all.
